lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 003: address reviewer finding

nextStoryContext: Fixed the reviewer-flagged stale/undated competitor claims in docs/positioning.md, section 3 (Competitive landscape). The finding: line 37's Orca star count ('Over 12,500 GitHub stars as of 2026-07') was measured at 29,274 stars on 2026-07-26 by the reviewer, roughly 2.3x low, despite carrying a current-month date label that implies freshness; and line 69's Spotify Honk claim ('over 1,500 pull requests') carried no date at all, though Spotify's own reporting had moved to a materially faster rate (1,000 merged PRs every 10 days) by March 2026. Root-cause fix (two edits, both in docs/positioning.md, no other file touched): (1) line 37: re-measured Orca's star count live via `curl https://api.github.com/repos/stablyai/orca` (29,283 stars on 2026-07-26, a live re-verification rather than trusting the stale reviewer-cited figure), replaced the undated-feeling 'as of 2026-07' phrasing with an explicit measurement method + date + a standing caveat that star counts move quickly and must be re-verified before reuse (matching the doc's own section 4.4 'Namespace facts (dated, not permanent)' convention for time-sensitive facts). (2) line 69: dated the 1,500-PR figure to its actual source month (Spotify's November 2025 engineering blog post, confirmed via web search), and added the QCon London 2026 (March 18, 2026, confirmed via WebFetch on the InfoQ writeup) follow-up figure showing the rate had accelerated from 1,000 merged PRs per 3 months (six months prior) to 1,000 merged PRs per 10 days, with an explicit sentence noting the November 2025 cumulative figure now understates current throughput. Both edits follow the pattern already established in section 4.4 of this same doc: date every time-sensitive claim and flag it as a point-in-time measurement, not a standing fact. Swept the diff for em-dash/emoji regressions post-edit (clean, zero matches introduced). No tests reference this doc's prose, so no test changes were needed.
